extracted.intended_audience: general readers, developers, researchers, and practitioners interested in feed/news aggregation
extracted.subtask_description: Survey of client software and web applications that aggregate digital content (news, blogs, podcasts, video) into a single interface, describing functions, types, technologies, and design/usage considerations. Useful as an overview for people building, evaluating, or choosing aggregator software or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation function / consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregation technology often consolidates (sometimes syndicated) web content into one page that can show only the new or updated information from many sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregators reduce the time and effort needed to regularly check websites for updates, creating a unique information space or 'personal newspaper'. The emphasis is on surfacing new/updated items from multiple sources in one view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported feed formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeds are often in the RSS or Atom formats which use Extensible Markup Language (XML) to structure pieces of information to be aggregated in a feed reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregators should support common XML feed formats (RSS, Atom, RDF/XML) to ensure broad compatibility with sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update/check behavior and subscription model
rubrics_metrics.description: Once subscribed to a feed, an aggregator is able to check for new content at user-determined intervals and retrieve the update. The content is sometimes described as being pulled to the subscriber, as opposed to pushed with email or instant messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/evaluate aggregators for configurable polling intervals, clear subscribe/unsubscribe mechanisms, and user control over update frequency; support for both pull and (where appropriate) push paradigms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ease of subscription (discovery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although some applications will have an automated process to subscribe to a news feed, the basic way to subscribe is by simply clicking on the web feed icon and/or text link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregators should make feed discovery and single-click subscription straightforward (web feed icons, copyable feed URLs, auto-detection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform trade-offs: desktop vs web-based
rubrics_metrics.description: Desktop applications offer the advantages of a potentially richer user interface and of being able to provide some content even when the computer is not connected to the Internet. Web-based feed readers offer the great convenience of allowing users to access up-to-date feeds from any Internet-connected computer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate platform choice by weighing richer offline-capable features (desktop) against portability and anytime access (web). Consider synchronization between platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration and embedding
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregation features are frequently built into web portal sites, in the web browsers themselves, in email applications, or in application software designed specifically for reading feeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregators that integrate with browsers, portals, or other apps can improve discoverability and workflow; consider plugins/extensions and API support for embedding widgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interface conventions (three-panel/email-like layout)
rubrics_metrics.description: The graphical user interface of such applications often closely resembles that of popular e-mail clients, using a three-panel composition in which subscriptions are grouped in a frame on the left, and individual entries are browsed, selected, and read in frames on the right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess UI for familiar, efficient reading patterns (folder/list/article panes), and options for customization (font size, density, article view vs headline view).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feed processing and personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Web aggregators gather material from a variety of sources for display in one location. They may additionally process the information after retrieval for individual clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for features that post-process feeds (filtering, translation, summarization, semantic indexing) and support personalization per user needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feed filtering and tagging to manage volume
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the problems with news aggregators is that the volume of articles can sometimes be overwhelming... many feed readers allow users to tag each feed with one or more keywords which can be used to sort and filter the available articles into easily navigable categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective filtering (tags, folders, rules), import of Attention Profiles, and search/sort are important to prevent overload; evaluate the granularity and automation of filtering tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated selection vs human curation
rubrics_metrics.description: News aggregation websites began with content selected and entered by humans, while automated selection algorithms were eventually developed to fill the content... Google News launched in 2002 using automated story selection, but humans could add sources..., while older Yahoo News used a combination of automated news crawlers and human editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating aggregation quality, consider source-selection method (algorithmic, editorial, hybrid), transparency of selection, and ability to add or exclude sources manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social news aggregator features (community engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social news aggregators collect the most popular stories on the Internet, selected, edited, and proposed by a wide range of people. Users submit news items, communicate with peers through direct messages and comments, and collaboratively select and rate submitted stories to get to a real-time compilation of what is currently perceived as 'hot'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important social features include submission UI, commenting, voting/rating, moderation, and mechanisms that surface community interest; measure engagement and controls against manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media/podcast support and enclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Media aggregators are client software or web-based applications which maintain subscriptions to feeds that contain audio or video media enclosures. They can be used to automatically download media, playback the media within the application interface, or synchronize media content with a portable media player.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For audio/video feeds evaluate automatic download, playback, bitrate support, enclosure handling, and sync/export to devices (podcatcher features).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcatching (BitTorrent via RSS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcatching is a mechanism that automatically downloads BitTorrent files advertised through RSS feeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supporting broadcatching, aggregators must handle torrent enclosures safely, manage storage/automation, and respect legal/ethical constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias- and framing-aware aggregation / analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame- and media-bias–aware news aggregators use automated methods and systems to analyze and show differences in coverage (e.g., extract key phrases that describe a topic differently) or matrix-based news aggregation spanning dimensions like source country vs reported country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bias-aware systems should provide explainable features (key-phrases, comparative matrices), enable cross-perspective views, and surface framing differences to users for more balanced consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensibility: OPML, widgets, Ajax, and mashups
rubrics_metrics.description: More advanced methods of aggregating feeds are provided via Ajax coding techniques and XML components called web widgets... they allow users to aggregate OPML files, email services, documents, or feeds into one interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregators that support import/export (OPML), widgets, APIs, and mashups enable portability and composition with other tools; evaluate openness and developer tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of aggregation for marketing and required UX
rubrics_metrics.description: RSS serves as a delivery mechanism for websites to push online content to potential users and as an information aggregator and filter for users. However, it has been pointed out that in order to push the content RSS should be user-friendly to ensure proactive interaction so that the user can remain engaged without feeling 'trapped', good design to avoid being overwhelmed by stale data, and optimization for both desktop and mobile use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For marketing use-cases, measure how well an aggregator or feed encourages engagement (clear calls-to-action, freshness), prevents overwhelm (design, stale-data handling), and works across devices (responsive, mobile-optimized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized aggregator use-cases (planet sites, community aggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are web applications that can be used to aggregate several blogs into one. One such variety—called planet sites—are used by online communities to aggregate community blogs in a centralized location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether aggregator supports multi-blog community aggregation, author attribution, chronological/chronological grouping, and community-level moderation/features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation formats (tickers, alerters, plugins/extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Software aggregators can also take the form of news tickers which scroll feeds like ticker tape, alerters that display updates in windows as they are refreshed, web browser macro tools or as smaller components (plugins or extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternative presentation modes (ticker, alerts, widgets, extensions) for different user workflows and device constraints; evaluate customization and intrusion level.
